about: Comment blocks with the code they sit on (the commentedCode item), 48 in all: 14 overclaims and 34 holds. The overclaims are comments reviews or fixes found claiming more than their code: the bones tunicWeights JSDoc (review-3 C2), encode.ts's 31 Mbps over a 37 Mbps bitrate (fixed in aaba2cff8), ask-store's doc on the wrong constant (p6-askname N4), aloneArgs' one-case-at-a-time (p6-truegate review-2), a knob post named by the level route (e433ae1e8), callers and hosts that were deleted (4a08d29e4), a board read's name promised the same in every lab (p6-transports review-3), ReviewFilms' choices (ea1a4fa4b) and launchArgs' same-pixels promise (p6-macgpu); 4 hand cases (a retry count, a concurrency, an atomic write, a lower-casing) fill the rest. The holds are near misses: the same comments after their fixes, and comments that state numbers the code has or derives (frames at a rate, dB, bytes, hsv of the hex given, bone lengths summed to the neck). Each real case's text is the item at the revision named.

cases.label: overclaims
cases.why: The JSDoc gives the shoulder ramps as 100..128 and 6..26; the code ramps smoothstep(80, 128, -y) and smoothstep(0, 33, |x|) (bones review-3 C2, round-3 o11).

Comment:
Chromium's software H.264 encoder (OpenH264) refuses quantizer rate
control ("Unsupported bitrate mode"), so it takes a bitrate. The master
asks for the rate the hardware master's quantizer 16 comes to: 31 Mbps
over righteousness-by-faith, keeping 82–87% of the paper's fine grain
(packages/film/README.md, "Encoders").

Code it sits on:
master: new Quality({ bitrate: 37_000_000, bitrateMode: 'variable' })
cases.why: The comment says the master asks for 31 Mbps; the code under it asks for 37_000_000 (fixed in aaba2cff8).

cases.label: overclaims
cases.text:
Comment:
Chrome's flags on `platform` (`process.platform`). On every platform the
2D canvas draws in software, so a frame's pixels are the same wherever it
is drawn, and WebGL (a look drawn in 3D, `canvas/gl.ts`, a `webgl2` rig)
runs on SwiftShader, Chrome's software GPU, asked for by name: Chrome is
withdrawing the fallback it takes to it unasked, and without it a 3D look
would draw its 2D fallback in a render, silently. On macOS the GPU process
runs too (`GPU_FLAG`: `tools/chrome.ts` spawns Chrome through the GPU
launcher, `tools/chrome-gpu.ts`, which drops the `--disable-gpu` Bun
spawns every Chrome with): it holds the hardware H.264 encoder a render
encodes with. WebGL stays on
SwiftShader there (`--use-angle=swiftshader`), not the Mac's GPU, so a 3D
look draws as the browser tests and a Linux render draw it. Elsewhere the
page encodes in software when it finds no hardware encoder
(`chooseEncoder`, player/encode.ts).

Code it sits on:
export const launchArgs = (platform: string): ReadonlyArray<string> => [
  '--disable-gpu-vsync',
  '--disable-frame-rate-limit',
  ...Arr.filter([GPU_FLAG, '--use-angle=swiftshader'], () => platform === 'darwin'),
  '--enable-unsafe-swiftshader',
  '--disable-accelerated-2d-canvas',
];
cases.why: Promises a frame's pixels are the same on every host; measured, 2D text differs by up to 210 levels between the Mac and Linux (p6-macgpu review-1 minor 5).

cases.label: holds
cases.text:
Comment:
Larger, to read at film scale, and still sincere: a bow, not a lean. The
chest and head keep the rig's small turns (0.055 and 0.18 rad); the chest
shortens to 0.84 and widens to 1.09, the shoulders round 0.22 rad down
from the neck and draw in to 0.94, the jaw squashes to 0.75 and the head
sinks with it (the chin stays on the neck), and the face slides down. The
lift overshoots to 1.07 along the chest and 1.1 on the jaw before it
settles.

Code it sits on:
export const AMPLIFIED: Gains = {
  chestAlong: 2,
  chestAcross: 2.5,
  jawAlong: 2.1,
  faceY: 1.6,
  faceSy: 1.5,
  nearY: 1.5,
  farY: 1.5,
  bodyY: 1.5,
};
cases.why: Each number follows from the gains over the rig's track: chest 1−2·0.08=0.84, across 1+2.5·0.035≈1.09, jaw 1−2.1·0.12≈0.75, lift 1.07 and 1.1.
